papers.title: Homogeneous polynomial approximation on symmetric convex bodies: A proof of Kro\'o's conjecture
papers.abstract: We resolve Kro\'o's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kro\'o's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights. Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization. We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.

papers.title: On a positivity conjecture of Fasi and Higham for Pad\'e approximants to the matrix exponential
papers.abstract: We study the positivity conjecture of Fasi and Higham [SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 40 (2019), Conjecture 3.2], which concerns the Taylor coefficients of the reciprocal of the denominator $q_{k,m}(z)$ of the Pad\'e approximant to the matrix exponential. The conjecture asserts that these coefficients are positive whenever $m$ is odd. We prove full positivity for $k=0$ and eventual positivity whenever the unique positive real zero of $q_{k,m}$ is the unique zero of minimal modulus. We also give an explicit computable sufficient threshold beyond which all coefficients are positive. Using Hermite scaling with leading-coefficient normalization, we prove that this spectral minimality holds for each fixed odd $m$ and all sufficiently large $k$. The unrestricted conjecture is nevertheless false. We give exact rational counterexamples and prove a transient scaling theorem showing that on the scale $n\asymp\sqrt{k+1}$ the normalized coefficients converge to an explicit oscillatory Hermite profile. For $m=5$ this profile is negative at one point, yielding infinitely many counterexamples. The counterexamples are not diagonal, and the diagonal case $k=m$, which is the case relevant in practice, remains open. These results do not imply a failure of the Fasi--Higham algorithm. Rather, they delimit the range in which the auxiliary positivity conjecture can be used as a theorem.

papers.title: Phase Retrieval of Bandlimited Signals Using a Morlet Wavelet and an Admissible Companion
papers.abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that complex bandlimited signals can be uniquely recovered (up to a global phase factor) from two families of wavelet transform magnitudes, sampled at twice the Nyquist rate in two frequency bins. These families come from translations of the fixed dilated Morlet wavelet and a fixed companion wavelet. The companion wavelet admits an augmented Morlet--Gaussian representation. We rewrite the two families as two modulated Gaussian convolution measurements of an auxiliary bandlimited signal. Using a Gaussian convolution uniqueness result, we prove that samples on \((4B)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\) determine every signal in \(PW_B^2\) (up to a global phase factor). Compared with earlier wavelet phase retrieval results, our approach requires significantly fewer sampling points.

papers.title: Inequalities, identities, and bounds for divided differences of the exponential function
papers.abstract: Let $\exp[x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n]$ denote the divided difference of the exponential function. (i) We prove that exponential divided differences, as functions of two nodes of arbitrary positive multiplicities with all other nodes fixed, are strictly sign-regular of all orders, with log-submodularity as the order-two case. We also establish strict supermodularity. (ii) We establish the four-point inequality $ \exp[a,a,b,c]\,\exp[d,d,b,c]+\exp[b,b,a,d]\,\exp[c,c,a,d]-\exp[a,b,c,d]^2 > 0 $ for all $ a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{R} $. Furthermore, we obtain a sharp quantitative generalization to arbitrarily many pairs of nodes, with additional common nodes allowed. (iii) We obtain sharp two-sided bounds for $\exp[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ at fixed mean and variance; as a consequence, we derive an asymptotic expansion for $n!\exp[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ as $n\to\infty$ for node sequences of bounded variance. (iv) We present closed-form identities for divided differences of the exponential function, including a convolution identity and summation formulas for repeated arguments.

papers.title: A time-map description of the one-dimensional (p,q)-Laplacian Fu\v{c}ik spectrum
papers.abstract: We study a one-dimensional Fu\v{c}ik-type boundary value problem (BVP) driven by the nonhomogeneous, one-dimensional $(p,q)$-Laplacian, \[ -\left(|u'|^{p-2}u' + |u'|^{q-2}u'\right)' = \lambda (u^+)^{p-1} - \mu (u^-)^{q-1}, \qquad u(0)=u(L)=0, \qquad L>0, \] where $1<q<p$ and $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb{R}$. The problem is asymmetric: the positive component is paired with the $p$-power and the negative component with the $q$-power. This asymmetry prevents the standard homogeneous $p$-Laplacian scaling argument from producing explicit Fu\v{c}ik curves. We first prove a quadrant reduction theorem. Any positive nodal interval for a solution forces $\lambda>0$, and any negative nodal interval forces $\mu>0$. Hence, all sign-changing solutions occur for values of $(\lambda,\mu)$ in the positive quadrant. Outside the positive quadrant, only one-sign solutions can occur. We also formulate the equation as an autonomous planar system and establish existence and uniqueness for its initial value problem in the positive quadrant. We then impose the second Dirichlet condition through a shooting formulation and show that every zero of a nontrivial Dirichlet solution is simple and isolated. This provides the dynamical foundation for the subsequent construction and gluing of nodal humps of solutions. Inside the positive quadrant, we use a classical one-dimensional time-map method to obtain a projected-geometry description of the spectrum, or the set of values of $(\lambda, \mu)$ for which there exist nontrivial solutions. Every nodal solution has a common energy $E>0$ shared by all positive and negative humps.

papers.title: Euler--Lagrange Flow Monotonicity for the Radon Transform
papers.abstract: We present a new gradient-like flow that targets critical points of the inequality for the planar Radon transform $\mathcal{R}$ proven by Oberlin and Stein, partially answering a question of Christ, who gave a complete characterisation of the extremisers of the inequality via rearrangement methods. We show that for non-negative radial initial data near the extremiser manifold, solutions to the flow exist globally and there exists a rescaled subsequence of the flow that converges to a critical point of the Radon functional $\|\mathcal{R} f\|_3/\|f\|_{3/2}$ locally in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We also obtain a quantitative result for the rate of decay of critical points, which complements a result of Christ arXiv:1106.0719 in the special case of radial functions. We prove a novel localised smoothing estimate for the operator $\mathcal{R}^*[(\mathcal{R}\cdot)^2]$ restricted to radial functions. This approach is complementary to that of Christ and provides a robust framework for studying extremal problems associated to Radon-like operators.

papers.title: Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
papers.abstract: We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(\sigma)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $\sigma$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

papers.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.

papers.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials
papers.abstract: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound. We present these consequences before the machinery. The main arguments simplify irrational-power finite-rank rigidity and give a Nash-curve ramification obstruction, stable under entire scalar additions, for powers, logarithms, and rational poles. The latter yields uniform finite supports on compact semialgebraic curves without assuming that the supports are semialgebraic. The known p-frame finite-replacement principle is distinguished from the extensions developed here. No unconditional discreteness theorem for general irrational p is claimed.

papers.title: The Borel transform of the WKB solution to the Pearcey system
papers.abstract: We study the system of partial differential equations which characterizes the Pearcey integral from the viewpoint of the exact WKB analysis. It is shown that the Borel transform of the WKB solutions to the system can be written as a linear combination of the branches of an algebraic function of degree $4$. Moreover, some connection formulas for the system are given.

papers.title: Generalised hyperbolic polynomials: combinatorial interpretation and real-rootedness
papers.abstract: For $p,q$ natural numbers, define $\Delta^{\langle p,q \rangle}:=x^{p-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y} + y^{q-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$, and consider the sequence of polynomials $\biggl((\Delta^{\langle p,q \rangle})^n \cdot x\biggr)_{n\geq 0}$; we call these the generalised hyperbolic polynomials. In this paper, we provide a simple combinatorial interpretation for these polynomials. As special cases, we obtain combinatorial interpretations for the coefficients of the analogs of sinh and cosh corresponding to the curve $x^p- p y^q/q=1$; on setting $p=q=3$, we obtain Conrad and Flajolet's tree interpretation for the coefficients of the Dixonian elliptic functions (2006) as a special case. Finally, we show that for any $p,q\geq 3$, after suitably normalising followed by substituting $y=1$, we obtain a sequence of univariate polynomials which are real-rooted.

papers.title: Diffraction of rotated measures
papers.abstract: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.

papers.title: Exponential decay of threshold correlations for symmetric periodic functions
papers.abstract: We study how often $n$ distinct integer dilates of a periodic function can all lie above a fixed threshold or all lie below its negative. We consider continuous functions $f:\mathbb R\to[-1,1]$ that are $1$-periodic, even, strictly decreasing on $[0,1/2]$, and satisfy $f(0)=1$ and $f(t+1/2)=-f(t)$. This class includes the cosine and the triangle wave. For $0\leq\alpha<1$, let $\rho_\alpha\in(0,1/4]$ be determined by $f(\rho_\alpha)=\alpha$, and let $F_\alpha(n)$ denote the infimum of these proportions over all sets of $n$ distinct positive integer frequencies. We prove that $F_\alpha(n)\geq 4\rho_\alpha^n$ and that the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}F_\alpha(n)^{1/n}$ exists for every threshold. When $\rho_\alpha^{-1}$ is an integer, we obtain \begin{align} F_\alpha(n) &\leq C_\alpha n^{\log_2((1-\rho_\alpha)/(1-2\rho_\alpha))}\rho_\alpha^n, \end{align} and hence the limit equals $\rho_\alpha$. Otherwise, the limit belongs to the interval $[\rho_\alpha,\lfloor\rho_\alpha^{-1}\rfloor^{-1}]$. The upper bound in the reciprocal case uses a cyclic covering construction previously studied in the context of circular graphs. We give a self-contained proof of the corresponding optimal modulus.

papers.title: Endpoint estimates for spherical maximal operators acting on radial functions in hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: In this article we investigate spherical maximal operators $\mathfrak m^\alpha$ of real order $\alpha$ acting on radial functions in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$. We show that for every $n\geq 2$, $1<p\leq\infty$ and $\alpha>(1-n)/2$, $\mathfrak m^\alpha$ is bounded on $L^p_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbb H^n)$ if and only if \begin{align*} \begin{cases} \alpha>1-n+\frac np, & 1<p\leq 2, \alpha>\frac1p-\frac{n-1}2, & 2<p\leq\frac{2n}{n-1}, \alpha\geq\frac{1-n}p, & p>\frac{2n}{n-1}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Moreover, we show that for $1<p\leq 2n/(n-1)$ and \begin{align*} \alpha= \begin{cases} 1-n+\frac np, & 1<p\leq 2, \frac1p-\frac{n-1}2, & 2<p\leq\frac{2n}{n-1}, \end{cases} \end{align*} $\mathfrak m^\alpha$ is bounded from $L^{p,1}_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbb H^n)$ to $L^{p,\infty}_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbb H^n)$.

papers.title: On $q$-middle convolution and generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation
papers.abstract: We investigate higher-order $q$-difference equations obtained by successive applications of a $q$-analogue of addition and the $q$-middle convolution. We construct an $n$-dimensional system of linear $q$-difference equations and derive a single $q$-difference equation whose coefficients are polynomials of degree at most $1$ in the independent variable. Under certain conditions on the parameters, the resulting equation is a generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation of order $n$. We also obtain a multiple Jackson integral representation of solutions and give sufficient conditions for its convergence. By suitably choosing the functions appearing in the integrand and specializing the parameters, we obtain $q$-hypergeometric series solutions of type ${}_n \phi_{n-1}$.

papers.title: Arithmetic classification of the Dirichlet eigenvalues for a one-dimensional nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problem
papers.abstract: We classify the arithmetic nature of the Dirichlet eigenvalues of a homogeneous nonlocal one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian problem with power-type nonlinearity $|u|^{q-2}u$. For rational $p,q>1$, either all eigenvalues are algebraic or all are transcendental. Algebraicity holds exactly when the interval length is an algebraic multiple of a distinguished scale determined by a beta value. This scale is transcendental. When $p=q$, the criterion reduces to algebraicity of the interval length divided by $\pi$,independently of the rational exponent.

papers.title: Matrix orthogonal polynomials related to diffference operators for $L$-orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: The difference operator $J$ arising from the higher order occurrence for the $L$-orthogonal polynomials is studied using various families of matrix orthogonal polynomials. The matrix orthogonal polynomials determine the polar decomposition of $J$ and its adjoint $J^\ast$ considered as operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$. The special case of symmetric $J$ leads to the case where the matrix polynomials reduce to diagonal matrix polynomials. The example of the symmetric case with constant coefficients for $L=2$ is discussed in detail.

papers.title: Approximating the poles of a Painlev\'e V transcendent for the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel
papers.abstract: The Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel has an expression as an integral containing a Painlev\'e transcendent $r$ satisfying Painlev\'e V, in the same way that the Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel has an expression involving the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlev\'e II. In this paper we use Pad\'e approximation to approximate the poles of this Painlev\'e transcendent $r$ in the complex plane. We use Pad\'e approximation near $0$, Hermite-Pad\'e approximation near $0$ and two-point Pad\'e approximation near $0$ and infinity.

papers.title: Sparse domination for $q$-variation associated with functional calculus
papers.abstract: We establish sparse domination for the $q$-variation of functional calculus families $\{\varphi(tL)\}_{t>0}$ on spaces of homogeneous type. Under generalized Gaussian estimates, we consider holomorphic multipliers of injective accretive operators, and Sobolev-type spectral multipliers of non-negative self-adjoint operators. For the Sobolev-type multipliers, we show that our regularity assumption is sharp in general except the endpoint. As corollaries, we obtain weighted $q$-variational estimates for Bochner-Riesz means and regularized Schr\"{o}dinger groups. Finally, we give several examples of operators to which our results apply.

papers.title: Uncertainty principles as forcing mechanisms
papers.abstract: In this note we first consider the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. We show that it acts as a {\bf forcing mechanism} in the following sense. Real functions that approach its limit are close to Gaussian distributions, with proximity both in the sense of total variation distance and Wasserstein-1 distance. We next consider the uncertainty principle for functions defined on finite Abelian groups, and show that it acts as a forcing mechanism in the following sense. Functions that approach its limit are close (after translation and modulation by a complex exponential) to indicator functions of some subgroup, with proximity measured in ${\mathbb {L}}^1$-norm.

papers.title: An involution for recurrences of Tricomi and other special functions
papers.abstract: Recently two new integrated recurrences were given for the Kummer function which together with the six recurrences already given in standard literature gave a total of eight recurrences, each one linking the baseline function to one of it's eight contiguous functions. Two new recurrences for the Tricomi function are given here which complete the set of eight recurrences for the Tricomi function linking it to it's contiguous functions. The involution presented previously is examined in detail for the recurrences of Cylinder, Associated Legendre and Kummer/Tricomi functions. This involution converts any given recurrence to a recurrence with the parameter shifts reversed, which creates conjugate pairs. One pair for Cylinder functions, two pairs for Associated Legendre functions and 4 pairs each for Kummer and Tricomi functions. Uniqueness is proven using Wronskians for the integrated recurrence relations, such that contiguous functions are single occupancy slots with only one integrated recurrence possible for each slot and for each independent solution of the ODE. For Cylinder and Associated Legendre functions this is simple, as the recurrences are identical for each independent solution. However, for Kummer and Tricomi functions the recurrences are different. This difficulty is bypassed using Gamma functions to scale the Tricomi recurrences to match the Kummer recurrences for each conjugate pair. It is not possible to match globally. This allows uniqueness to be proven using Wronskians on a pair by pair basis. Hence the involution system behaves like a Pauli Exclusion principle for contiguous functions, with only one recurrence possible for each solution of the ODE.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Online-Compression Approach to Proportional Subsets of Bounded Orthonormal Systems
papers.abstract: Let $(\phi_i)_{i=1}^n$ be an orthonormal system on a probability space with $\|\phi_i\|_\infty\leq L$. We prove that, for every $2\leq k<n$, there is a set $I$ of at least $n-k$ indices such that $$ \|f\|_2\leq CM_k\sqrt{\log(e+M_k)}\|f\|_1 $$ for every $f$ in the span of $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$, where $M_k=L\sqrt{\frac{n}{k}\log(2k)}$. This replaces the logarithmic exponent $\frac{5}{2}$ in the corresponding theorem of Gu\'edon, Mendelson, Pajor, and Tomczak-Jaegermann by $\frac{1}{2}$. We also obtain a partition into two sets of cardinality $\frac{n}{2}+O(\sqrt n)$ for which both spans satisfy the resulting norm comparison, and for uniformly bounded systems the proportional estimate is $C\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}$ for sufficiently large $n$. This is the third paper in a series systematically using gradient descent as a proof mechanism in harmonic analysis, following the $\Lambda(p)$ and Bernoulli restricted isometry papers of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause, and the descent here is entropic mirror descent. We represent each function in an $L_1$ ball by a probability measure of controlled relative entropy, and this entropy pays for the corrections to the predictions of its coefficients. Processing the thresholds from large to small, we obtain a single weighted bound for all the corrections, which we turn into a finite description of approximate coefficient squares and then into a conditional Rademacher estimate, and symmetrization completes the argument directly on the $L_1$ ball. We also record consequences for concentration and for recovery from coefficient measurements.

papers.title: Sparse domination and an extended $L^p$ range for the trilinear Hilbert transform
papers.abstract: We establish sparse bounds for the trilinear Hilbert transform $$ T(f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):=\textrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-t)f_2(x-2t)f_3(x-3t)\,\frac{dt}{t}, $$ with averaging exponents arbitrarily close to $2$ from above. As a consequence, we extend OpenAI's $L^3\times L^3\times L^3\to L^1$ bound (entry 086 in the OpenAI Research Catalog) to $L^{p_1}\times L^{p_2}\times L^{p_3}\to L^r$ throughout the range $$ 2<p_1,p_2,p_3<\infty, \qquad \frac1r=\frac1{p_1}+\frac1{p_2}+\frac1{p_3}, \qquad \frac23<r<2, $$ and obtain corresponding weighted estimates for weights in multilinear Muckenhoupt classes. Our proof relies on the normalized local estimate and stopping time argument developed in OpenAI's work.

papers.title: Sharp derivative inequalities for maximal functions
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal constant in the $L^p$-derivative inequality for the uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on the real line for every $1<p<\infty$. It is the unique number $\gamma_p\in [0,1]$ satisfying $(2p-1)\gamma_p+(p-1)\gamma_p^{(2p-1)/(p-1)}=p$. As $p$ goes from $1$ to $+\infty$, $\gamma_p$ decreases from $1$ to $\sqrt2-1$, and at the endpoints the limiting arguments recover the classical total-variation and Lipschitz inequalities, with the qualitative regularity ingredient at the $BV$ endpoint supplied by Aldaz and P\'erez L\'azaro.

papers.title: A Sharp Bound of Crossing Limit Cycle for Planar piecewise linear Systems with a Straight Switching Line
papers.abstract: Determining the maximum number of crossing limit cycles in planar discontinuous piecewise linear systems separated by a straight line is a central problem in nonsmooth dynamical systems and a natural piecewise-linear counterpart of Hilbert's sixteenth problem, yet its sharp uniform upper bound has long remained an open problem. In this paper, we prove that any such system admits at most three crossing limit cycles. Combined with known examples realizing three crossing limit cycles, this result establishes that three is the sharp uniform upper bound.

papers.title: On certain mapping properties of a weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: In this article, we study a weighted analogue of the totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space. Throughout the article, we are concerned with the mapping properties of this transform. Particularly, we first consider the existence of the operator on weighted Lebesgue spaces, where the weights under consideration are natural to the geometry of the hyperbolic space. Then, we proceed to see the $L^p$-improving mapping properties of the said transform on radial functions. Further, we also prove end-point boundedness results on Lorentz spaces of radial functions. Lastly, we look into the problem of weighted $L^p$-$L^p$ boundedness, and obtain partial results in this direction. In the way of obtaining these results, we also give a spherical integral representation of the weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform.

papers.title: Inverse scattering problem for the fifth-order Schr${\rm\bf\ddot{o}}$dinger operator on the whole axis
papers.abstract: A method of solution for the inverse scattering problem for the linear fifth order Schr${\rm\ddot{o}}$dinger operator is found. Two closed systems of linear singular integral equations are obtained. From solutions to these equations, potential on the left and right half-axes is restored unambiguously.

papers.title: $L^p$ integrability of functions with Fourier support on High codimension manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $n,k\ge 2$ and $N_{n,k} = \binom{n+k}{k}-1$. We prove that if $f \in L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{N_{n,k}})$ and $\hat{f}$ is supported on the $n$-dimensional Parsell-Vinogradov manifold, then $f \equiv 0$ whenever $1\le p < p_{c}(n,k) = n+ \binom{n+k}{n+1}$. This improves the bound by Agranovsky and Narayanan, and generalizes the moment-curve result of Guo-Iosevich-Zhang-Zorin-Kranich. The exponent $p_{c}(n,k)$ is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$, since it matches the convergence exponent $p_{n,k}^{\mathrm{Tar}}$ of Tarry's problem. Our result also yields a general lower bound $p_{n,k}^{\mathrm{Tar}} \ge p_{c}(n,k)$, improving Ikromov's bound by $n-1$. The proof combines the rotation symmetry of Parsell-Vinogradov manifold with the essential orthogonality of rotated covering boxes.

papers.title: A complete theory of local minimizers for periodic variational problems
papers.abstract: We study the periodic problem in the Calculus of Variations and give a complete characterization of the positive definiteness of the second variation, extending the Reid Roundabout Theorem to periodic boundary conditions. Two formulations are established: one in terms of conjugate and semi-coupled points, and one in terms of the existence of a symmetric solution of the associated Riccati equation satisfying a boundary inequality. We show by an explicit example that the latter condition, while sufficient, is not necessary except in dimension one. As applications, we obtain sufficient conditions for weak and strong local minimizers of periodic solutions of the Euler-Lagrange equation.

papers.title: The S-function at arbitrary order: hyperplanes of symmetries and the realisability condition
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
papers.abstract: For a scalar equation $y^{(n)}=\varphi(x,y,\dots,y^{(n-1)})$ the $S$-function of the extended Prelle--Singer method is a vector $S=(S_0,\dots,S_{n-2})$, the null-form vector of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Lakshmanan and collaborators, and the jet gradient of a first integral solves the adjoint of the variational equation. We describe the solutions of the system satisfied by $S$ intrinsically, and determine which of them come from first integrals. Over the field $C$ of first integrals the solutions are exactly the hyperplanes of the $n$-dimensional space $VV$ of symmetry characteristics, recovered from $n-1$ independent characteristics by a Pl\"ucker formula; in flow-box coordinates they are the hyperplane fields on the local space of leaves. A solution is the $S$-vector of a first integral if and only if the corresponding hyperplane field is integrable. This Frobenius condition splits into the $S$-system itself plus $\binom n3$ further differential conditions, so it is vacuous for $n=2$ and a genuine restriction for every $n\ge3$, for which we give an explicit non-realisable solution. The same picture explains why $\lambda$-symmetries and $S$-functions coincide only when $n=2$: line fields and hyperplane fields agree only on surfaces. For the computation of $S$ we record that the system is equivalent to one scalar equation for the last component, which is the Riccati form of the adjoint variational equation, and we spell out what this does and does not imply for a rational search.
